title: Metabolic Profiling of Antigen-Specific CD8+ T Cells Using Spectral Flow Cytometry
author: de Graaf, J. Fréderique
materials: Note: Take care to avoid spills, as human-derived materials should be treated as potentially hazardous.
Surface staining with tetramer in unstimulated/resting cells
Intracellular staining of cells after peptide stimulation

Note: Numerous metabolic antibodies are commercially available, however, many are not pre-conjugated to fluorophores. Several antibody labeling kits allow rapid conjugation of the antibody of interest within 3.5 h. Regardless of the method used, each newly generated antibody–fluorophore conjugate must be carefully titrated prior to experimental use to ensure optimal signal-to-noise performance.
Acquire the experimental samples and optional batch controls.

steps.title: Pre‑cool PBS
steps.instruction: Place PBS at 4 °C before any cell handling.

steps.title: Generate single‑cell suspension
steps.instruction: Create a single‑cell suspension from either buffy coat or spleen tissue.

substeps.instruction: Buffy coat: Transfer 20 mL buffy coat into a 50 mL tube and add 30 mL cold PBS.
Spleen: Mechanically dissociate ~1 cm³ human spleen through a 70 µm cell strainer into a 50 mL tube and add 30 mL cold PBS.
Process spleen‑derived cells identically to PBMCs after this step.

steps.title: Initial centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the suspension at 300 × g for 15 min at 4 °C and carefully decant the supernatant.

steps.title: Prepare Ficoll gradient
steps.instruction: Add 15 mL Ficoll‑Paque to each 50 mL tube (one tube per donor).

steps.title: Layer cells onto Ficoll
steps.instruction: Resuspend the cell pellet in 30 mL PBS, then gently layer the suspension on top of the Ficoll while maintaining a clear interface.

steps.title: Correct disturbed interface
steps.instruction: If the interface is disturbed, wash the cells 2–3 times with PBS (300 × g, 5 min, 4 °C) and repeat the layering step until the interface is intact.

steps.title: Density‑gradient centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 500 × g for 20 min, no brake, 4 °C.

steps.title: Collect lymphocyte layer
steps.instruction: Carefully collect the white, cloudy lymphocyte layer at the plasma‑Ficoll interphase and transfer it to a new 50 mL tube.

steps.title: Wash lymphocytes
steps.instruction: Fill the tube to maximum volume with PBS, centrifuge at 300 × g for 10 min at 4 °C, then discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Resuspend in complete medium
steps.instruction: Resuspend the cell pellet in 10 mL complete medium.

substeps.instruction: If using frozen PBMCs, rest them 2–16 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ in a T25 flask containing complete medium supplemented with 30 µg/mL DNAse I (type IV).

steps.title: Count and adjust cell concentration
steps.instruction: Determine viable cell number using Trypan Blue (or an automated counter) and adjust the suspension to 10 × 10⁶ cells mL⁻¹.

steps.title: Plate cells for analysis
steps.instruction: Plate 1 × 10⁶ cells per well in 100 µL complete medium in a 96‑well plate.

substeps.instruction: Use a round‑bottom (U‑bottom) plate for ≥1 × 10⁶ cells per well; use a conical (V‑bottom) plate for <1 × 10⁶ cells per well.
Plate each sample in triplicate; include a negative control, a positive control, and a peptide‑stimulated condition.
Prepare single‑stain reference controls: 1 × 10⁶ cells per well for (i) unstained control, (ii) live/dead control, and (iii) one well per fluorophore (cells or beads).

steps.title: Add stimulation reagents
steps.instruction: Prepare the three stimulation conditions for each triplicate set.

substeps.instruction: Negative control: add 100 µL complete medium (no stimulant).

Positive control (PMA/ionomycin): add 100 µL complete medium containing PMA 25 ng mL⁻¹ and ionomycin 0.25 µg mL⁻¹ (add 0.5 µL PMA from a 10 µg mL⁻¹ stock and 0.5 µL ionomycin from a 100 µg mL⁻¹ stock).
Peptide stimulation: add 100 µL complete medium containing peptide to a final 5 µg mL⁻¹ (e.g., 1 µL of 1 mg mL⁻¹ HCMV pp65₄95‑503 peptide to 99 µL medium).

steps.title: Incubate cells
steps.instruction: Incubate the plates for 16–20 h at 37 °C in a humidified 5 % CO₂ incubator.

substeps.instruction: Shorter or longer incubations (12–144 h) may be used depending on the experimental question.

steps.title: Transfer to round‑bottom plate if needed
steps.instruction: If a flat‑bottom plate was used, transfer the cells to a U‑bottom or V‑bottom plate before downstream staining.

steps.title: Live/Dead staining
steps.instruction: Stain cells with Zombie Aqua (Live/Dead) dye.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 1:1000 dilution of the dye in cold PBS (e.g., 1 µL dye + 1000 µL PBS).
Add 50 µL diluted dye to each well and incubate 15 min at 4 °C protected from light.

steps.title: Wash after viability stain
steps.instruction: Add 150 µL ice‑cold PBS, centrifuge 400 × g for 5 min at 4 °C, discard supernatant.

steps.title: Fc receptor blocking
steps.instruction: Block Fc receptors to reduce non‑specific binding.

substeps.instruction: Prepare FcBlock: mix 2.5 µL Human TruStain FcX with 500 µL FACS buffer (sufficient for 10 samples).
Add 50 µL FcBlock to each well and incubate 10 min on ice (or in the fridge).

steps.title: Wash after Fc block
steps.instruction: Add 150–200 µL cold FACS buffer, centrifuge 400 × g for 4 min at 4 °C, discard supernatant.

steps.title: Prepare surface antibody/tetramer mix
steps.instruction: Make the appropriate surface‑staining cocktail (unstimulated or peptide‑stimulated).

substeps.instruction: Unstimulated (Table 1) per 10 samples (total 300 µL):

FACS buffer 138.4 µL, Brilliant Stain buffer 138.4 µL, αCD8‑APC‑Fire8 0.19 µL (1:1600), αCD25‑BV711 1.5 µL (1:200), αCD3‑BUV395 3 µL (1:50), αCD45RA‑BUV496 0.19 µL (1:1600), αCD197‑BV785 6 µL (1:50), HLA‑A*01 tetramer (APC) 6 µL (1:50), HLA‑A*02 tetramer (APC) 6 µL (1:50), Dasatinib 0.3 µL (final 0.05 µM, 1:1000).
Peptide‑stimulated (Table 2) per 10 samples (total 300 µL):
FACS buffer 138.4 µL, Brilliant Stain buffer 138.4 µL, αCD25‑BV711 1.5 µL (1:200), αCD69‑Percp‑Cy5.5 3 µL (1:50), αCD38‑APC‑Fire8 6 µL (1:50), αCD137‑BV650 6 µL (1:50).
Use the same dilutions for single‑stain reference controls (cells or beads).

steps.title: Surface staining
steps.instruction: Add 30 µL of the appropriate antibody/tetramer mix to each well and incubate 30 min at 4 °C in the dark.

substeps.instruction: If tetramers are included, incubation at room temperature for 15 min on 37 °C can improve staining; adjust accordingly.

steps.title: Wash after surface stain
steps.instruction: Wash cells twice with 150–200 µL cold FACS buffer, centrifuging 400 × g for 4 min at 4 °C each time, discarding supernatant after each wash.

steps.title: Prepare fixation buffer
steps.instruction: Make fixation/permeabilization buffer (4× dilution).

substeps.instruction: Mix 250 µL Fixation/Permeabilization solution (eBioscience FoxP3 kit) with 750 µL Perm Diluent (final 4×; dilution may range 4×–16× depending on target).

steps.title: Fix cells
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL fixation buffer to each well, gently resuspend, and incubate 45 min at 20 °C in the dark (30–60 min acceptable).

steps.title: Wash after fixation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge 500 × g for 5 min at 20 °C, discard supernatant, then wash twice with 150–200 µL permeabilization buffer.

substeps.instruction: Prepare permeabilization buffer: 1 mL Perm Buffer 10× (FoxP3 kit) + 9 mL Milli‑Q water.
Each wash: add buffer, centrifuge 500 × g for 5 min at 20 °C, discard supernatant.

steps.title: Prepare intracellular antibody mix
steps.instruction: Make the intracellular staining cocktail appropriate for the experimental condition.

substeps.instruction: Unstimulated (Table 3) per 10 samples (total 300 µL): Perm buffer 294 µL, αKi‑67‑PE‑Dazzle594 1.5 µL (1:200), αGLUT1‑Dylight405 0.5 µL (1:600), αPKM‑PE 0.75 µL (1:400), αG6PD‑APC‑Cy7 0.5 µL (1:800), αCPT1a‑PE‑Cy5.5 0.5 µL (1:600), αATP5a‑FITC 0.5 µL (1:600), αSDHA‑AF647 0.15 µL (1:2000), αGlutaminase‑PE‑Cy7 0.5 µL (1:600).

Peptide‑stimulated (Table 4) per 10 samples (total 300 µL): Perm buffer 294 µL, αCytochrome C‑PE‑Cy7 0.5 µL (1:600), αCD98‑BUV395 0.75 µL (1:400), αG6PD‑APC‑Cy7 0.5 µL (1:800), αATP5a‑FITC 0.5 µL (1:600), αSDHA‑AF647 0.15 µL (1:2000).
Use recommended dilutions for single‑stain reference controls (Tables 3 and 4).

steps.title: Intracellular staining
steps.instruction: Add 30 µL intracellular antibody mix (or 30 µL single‑stain control) to each well and incubate 30–45 min at 20 °C in the dark.

substeps.instruction: Longer incubation can improve signal intensity.

steps.title: Wash after intracellular stain
steps.instruction: Wash twice with 150 µL 1× permeabilization buffer, centrifuge 500 × g for 5 min at 20 °C, discard supernatant each time.

steps.title: Final resuspension for acquisition
steps.instruction: Resuspend each well in 100–150 µL FACS buffer and keep on ice until acquisition.

steps.title: Create mixed single‑stain reference
steps.instruction: Combine 10 µL of each single‑stained control, 10 µL unstained control, and 10 µL viability‑dye control into one tube for spectral unmixing verification.

steps.title: Spectral flow cytometer setup
steps.instruction: Run start‑up and quality‑control procedures on the spectral analyzer.

steps.title: Acquire control samples
steps.instruction: Open a new experiment, adjust FSC/SSC, and acquire single‑stain, unstained, and live/dead controls.

substeps.instruction: Collect ≥50 000 events for cell samples and ≥5 000 events for bead controls.

steps.title: Perform spectral unmixing
steps.instruction: Unmix the acquired single‑stain data using the software.

steps.title: Verify unmixing with mixed reference
steps.instruction: Acquire the mixed single‑stain reference sample and confirm accurate unmixing.

steps.title: Acquire experimental samples
steps.instruction: Acquire all experimental wells (triplicates, controls, etc.) on the spectral flow cytometer.

steps.title: Check and adjust unmixing
steps.instruction: After acquisition, review the unmixing; adjust the matrix if needed using the mixed reference sample.

steps.title: Data analysis
steps.instruction: Apply appropriate gating (≥50 000 events per sample), adjust scales, and perform downstream analyses such as opt‑tSNE, histogram, and statistical testing.
